source.question: F-12's water cut fell from about 0.97 to about 0.3 at the end of 2014. What was done to the well, and why did the plug set in 2010 not do the same?

note: Reviewed Oct 29: fair rejections (undeclared numbers, a gradual shift written as a fall at a date, causes marked fact, a limit said to hold that did not). False problems found here and fixed: a depth pair written [3147,3161] in a detail, a share tied to a depth in another plug's clause, 'water ~92.5%' read as a water cut, a range's top depth. One strict by design: '1%' of the 3,220 m row under 'e.g. at 3,200 m'.

submission.summary: Re-check keeps the 2014 result but clarifies it: F-12’s water cut fell from about 0.97 to about 0.31 after the 32-day workover that set a plug at 3150 m and opened a new zone, most likely because that depth is just above the water entry seen on the earlier log. The 2010 plug at 3210 m was too deep to block that water, and its small rise then was the ongoing trend, not a gauge or field effect; the 2014 gain persisted on decline, not as a short flush.

findings.claim: F-12 was shut in for 32 days from 2014-11-30 for a workover that set a plug at 3150 m and perforated a new zone above it.
findings.detail: Job 2014-11-22 to 2014-11-27: 2014-11-26 Installed 7" EVO plug with mid element at 3150 m. Perforated new zone from 3126,2-3139,7 mMD (perforations recorded as 3126.2-3130.7 mMD). Shut-in 2014-11-30 to 2014-12-31, 32 days, field-wide with F-1 C, F-15 D.

findings.claim: Across that workover the well’s water cut fell from 0.965 to 0.338 and oil rose to 857 Sm3/d.
findings.detail: plugs_set for 2014-11-26 depth 3150 m: before window 2014-09-23 to 2014-11-22 water_cut 0.965 oil 177 Sm3/d (60 days), after window 2014-11-29 to 2015-01-28 water_cut 0.338 oil 857 Sm3/d (28 days). Monthly data: 2014-11 water_cut 0.9623, 2014-09 0.9672, 2015-01 water_cut 0.3107.

findings.claim: The 2010 plug at 3210 m left water cut almost unchanged from 0.638 to 0.676 in its 60-day window; averaged over 3 months before and after it rose only from 0.626 to 0.689.

The larger water-cut rise flagged around 2010-10-24 was a gradual trend, not a step at the plug: its mean shifted from 0.513 to 0.814 over the whole period but only from 0.65 to 0.69 across the 4 weeks around the date with choke steady.
findings.detail: E3 regime_change water_cut 2010-10-24: before_mean 0.5134 after_mean 0.8141 change 0.3006, across_before 0.6455 across_after 0.6867 change_across 0.04121, period 2010-02-14 to 2016-08-14. Daily choke ~53% on 2010-10-12-24, so no choke move explains it. Sensor failure interval 2010-10-12 to 2016-09-17 with 0 reading on 2095 days but flowing 1830 days and 1,133,053 Sm3 oil.

findings.claim: The 2014 water-cut fall was specific to F-12’s workover, not a field choke or injection change: liquid rate and choke fell only at F-12 while field voidage stayed near 1.02 and neighbors stayed watery or dry.
findings.detail: F-12 monthly liquid 4923 Sm3/d at 100% choke in 2014-11 to 1251 Sm3/d at 30% choke in 2015-01, then back to 100% by 2015-06 with water_cut 0.63 rising gradually. F-1 C 2014-11 water_cut 0.5188 liquid 577 choke 50.93, 2014-12 still 0.604; F-15 D 2014-11 water_cut 0.039. Field voidage replacement_ratio 2014 1.02, 2015 0.9995, injected 3,825,493 to 3,201,627 Sm3, so injection kept pace.

findings.claim: On the 2010-09 log the deep plug would cut only about 33% of the water and about 1% of the oil, while a plug at 3150 m would cut about 97% of the water.
findings.detail: PLT 2010-09 low rate: below 3210 m oil 0.011 water 0.325; below 3150 m oil 0.808 water 0.971. Medium rate: below 3210 m oil 0.015 water 0.376; below 3150 m oil 0.734 water 1.0. Oil comes in 3132-3165 m, water 3165-3243 m, so 3150 m sits just above main water entry.

findings.claim: The 2014 plug depth relies on a log 4 years old with no post-job log, but the oil gain persisted as a steady decline rather than a flush.
findings.detail: Latest PLT 2010-09-22, 2151 days before 2016-08-12, water_cut then 0.6307 now 0.8779, so inflow may have moved. No post-2014 PLT exists. Decline fit 2015-01-02 to 2016-08-12 exponential r2_log 0.9535 qi 958.67 Sm3/d di 1.16 per year, 577 points, uptime 0.9751, shows sustained production above pre-workover low (~177 Sm3/d). New perf 3126.2-3130.7 mMD is in upper oil zone; 81% oil below 3150 m on old log was therefore expected but replaced.

RIH with 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 800 m.
Installed 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 3210 m mid element. RD wireline pressure control equipment and handed well over to production department.
Spotted some equpment. Waited on weather, wind above 40 knots.
Spotted WL equipment. Checked equipment together with rig electrician.
Spotted equipment. Well handed over from Production dept. to D&W. Started to rig up on wellhead.

Completed rigging up wireline equipment. Leak tested rig up to 20/345 bar. Run in hole with Halliburton EVO plug. Pulled out of hole after tool failure at 1400 m. Started to prepare back up toolstring.
Installed 7" EV0 plug with mid element at 3150 m. Perforated new zone from 3126,2 -3139,7 mMD. POOH with perforating gun.
POOH with perfoartion gun. Inflow tested well barriers. Rigged down WL equipment. Operation completed.

result.note: Daily reports exist for drilling and for work on the well (wireline, plugs, perforations, production logs), not for days of normal production. A job's date is the day the work was done; kind is drilling, completion, workover (work on a producing or injecting well) or abandonment. Ask for one day to see every operation line.

surveys.read_from: LAS files of the interpreted log (Well_logs_pr_WELL/15_9-F-12/10.PRODUCTION LOGS/PLT Sept 2010)

result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove, not what it did; plugs_set gives what each plug already set did to the well (water cut and oil before and after). A bridge plug is set in blank pipe, never inside a perforated interval (inside_perforation_m names the interval a depth falls in; blank_pipe_m lists the gaps, and each pass's at_blank_pipe gives the shares below the top and the bottom of every gap: the depths a plug can actually be set at). since_survey says how old the latest log is and how far the water cut has moved since: an old log may no longer show where the water enters, and a new one would settle it. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.

Performed three correlation passes across interval 3135 - 3050 m. Positioned gun with top shot at 3126,2 m & bottom shot at 3130,7 mMD. WHP 45 bar.

result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. arguments.sql: SELECT date, well, bhp_bar, water_cut, oil_sm3, water_sm3, choke_pct FROM production_daily WHERE well='F-12' AND date BETWEEN '2010-09-01' AND '2010-11-30' ORDER BY date
